# New

A package in scope has no `pipelines.md`. Read `steps.md` (rules) and `template.md` (the file format) here; `examples-new.md` has two worked New rounds. Ends at the Review Gate in `../SKILL.md`.

```
STATUS ─→ WORKFLOWS (ask) ─→ STEPS ─→ LAYOUT ─→ WRITE ─→ [gate: stop]
```

**1. Workflows.** Confirm them with the user as `../SKILL.md` (Asking about workflows) says.

**2. Steps.** Per pipeline, following `steps.md`: an ID from `dt next-id PL` (write the section before the next; never count by hand), Entry, Trigger, Covers, a step table with one owner, `In → Out` in contract types and a real spine version per step, and a pre-build entry sketch of step calls only.

**3. Layout.** One entry module per component or package, one module per step owner, each under `build-setup`'s size bar (`steps.md`, Layout).

**4. Write** `docs/packages/<pkg>/pipelines.md` from `template.md`, each pipeline about 35 lines (`dt lint` `budget`). Append the calling PL IDs to each called contract symbol's `Used by:` line (`- **Used by:** portfolio; PL-02, PL-03`); that leaves an Approved contract Approved. A step needing a different signature, type or error is a contract change: list it and route to `architecture-design` Revise. Fix what `dt lint` reports on every file touched.

steps.text:
Approvals done. Before writing the pipelines, I need you to confirm which workflows you'll actually run.

**What's done:**
- **Approved:** the architecture and contract are marked Approved, with all 12 decisions now Accepted. Your two choices (staying single-package, and deciding the padding question during S2) already match what the doc says, so no text changed.
- **Committed:** as `bdd9c1c` on the branch `docs/brief-and-roadmap`. Your auto-commit had already picked up the earlier changes, so this commit only marks the docs Approved.
- **dataviz is not installed in the project.** It's a skill built into Claude Code, and there are no files on this machine I can copy into `.claude/skills/`. It works in every Claude Code session, so later stages can still use it; only the plugin's lint check warns that it isn't installed. I didn't recreate it by hand, because a partial copy would drift from the real one. If you have a copy of the skill's source, I can install it from that.

**Proposed workflows.** Each becomes one pipeline: one command you run, made of named steps. Nothing is written until you confirm.

| # | Workflow | Trigger | What it does | Stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Train** | `rllab train <config> [--seeds 0-4]` | Loads the configuration, then builds the worlds and learners. It runs training (one or two teams), logs, saves checkpoints and Phase B snapshots, and writes the run folder. With several seeds, it runs one process per seed | S1, used again in S2 and S3 |
| 2 | **Train reference** | `rllab reference <config> --seeds 0-4` | Trains the Stable-Baselines3 learner on the same world and budget, into the same run-folder format | S1 (also S2, S3 Phase A) |
| 3 | **Evaluate & compare** | `rllab compare <config>` | Scores the final checkpoints and baselines on test seeds and writes the per-seed comparison table and the 80% reference check. Then you run the `null-hypothesis-testing` skill on the table | S1 |
| 4 | **Watch** | `rllab view <policy> [<policy2>] --seed N` | Records an episode from each checkpoint or baseline and plays one, or two side by side | S1 |
| 5 | **Lesson note** | `rllab note <world>` / `rllab status <world>` | Draws the learning-curve and diagnostic charts, refreshes the note's generated blocks, and reports whether the world is done | S1 |
| 6 | **Cross-play** | `rllab crossplay <phase-b-run>` | Plays every prey snapshot against every predator snapshot and writes the 11×11 table, the heatmap, and the comparison table for PREY-15 | S3 |

These cover every stage, so the whole roadmap gets designed now, before any build planning. **My recommendation is all six.** Reply "all six", or tell me which to drop, merge or add. For example, Watch and Lesson note could become one command.
